newsitem.title: USA: Airline stocks rise after Goldman Sachs upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Airline stocks rise after Goldman Sachs upgrades.

text.p: U.S. airline stocks rose Thursday amid a convergence of favorable developments, including Goldman Sachs raising its ratings on two issues.
In addition, investors became more optimistic that the proposed alliance between British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines would be approved, analysts said.

"There's really a number of things going on....There was some positive news flow on the BA-AMR pact on both sides of the Atlantic. And it looks to be the end of Goldman's selling on US Airways. Goldman also upgraded the stock today, which helped," said Timothy Ross, an analyst with SBC Warburg.

Goldman Sachs said it crossed a block trade of 3.5 million shares of US Airways Group Inc at 34-1/2, up 1-5/8. Goldman Sachs and US Airways did not immediately return calls seeking comment on the trade.
On May 22, British Airways entered a pact with Goldman Sachs to sell the carrier's remaining 14.46 million shares of US Airways for $499 million, or $34.50 a share.
On Thursday, US Airways benefited as Goldman Sachs analyst Glenn Engel raised his rating on the stock to trading buy from market outperform. US Airways was up 2 to 34-7/8 in late afternoon trading.
Engel also placed Continental Airlines Inc on the recommended list, raising his rating on that stock from from market outperform. Continental's B shares were 1 higher at 35-1/2.
Shares of AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, were 1-1/4 higher at 99-1/4. American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of British Airways added 3-3/4 to 117-5/8.
After hearings in Washington on Wednesday, investors were more optimistic that the proposed BA-AMR alliance would gain approval, analysts said.

Investors viewed a proposal by the General Accounting Office on allocating slots at London's Heathrow Airport as a positive development, analysts said. The GAO on Wednesday outlined a plan under which six U.S. airlines competing with the proposed BA-AMR alliance would gain 23 slots at Heathrow.
The GAO plan was seen as a compromise that could increase the chances of the proposed alliance being approved, analyst said.
Airlines stocks were also bolstered Thursday by robust May traffic reports by several large carriers, analysts said.
